classification.difficultyReason: Connect the linear scale factor to an area multiplier of sixteen, then multiply and simplify the smaller rectangle's surd dimensions.

content.prompt:
These rectangles are similar. The scale factor is 4.
Find the area of $B$ in its simplest form.

spec.description: Paired unshaded horizontal rectangles with smaller A to the left and larger B to the right, their top edges aligned. Dimensions of A remain to its left and beneath it. Drawn sizes are schematic.
spec.mathematics: Rectangle A has height sqrt(3) cm and width sqrt(6) cm. The stated linear scale factor from A to B is 4.
spec.answerVisibility: Only A's supplied dimensions and the labels A and B are visible.

answer.worked:
An enlargement with scale factor $4$ multiplies area by $4^{2}=16$.
$$\begin{align*}A_A&=\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{6}\\&=\sqrt{18}\\&=3\sqrt{2}\ \mathrm{cm}^{2}\\A_B&=16\times3\sqrt{2}\\&=48\sqrt{2}\ \mathrm{cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$
